 USL League One Announces 2026 Awards Finalists
 By USLLeagueOne.com Staff , 11/06/26, 12:00PM EST 
 Share 
 Top Players, Coaches earn nomination after standout regular season campaigns
 TAMPA, Fla. – USL League One announced today the finalists for the 2026 USL League One Awards, with the leading performers in five categories earning nominations after impressive 2026 regular season campaigns. The award winners will be announced between Monday, November 9 and Friday, November 13.  
 Seven of the award finalists will appear in the Semifinals of the 2026 USL League One Playoffs this weekend, with the Charlotte Independence’s Head Coach Mike Jeffries, goalkeeper Matt Levy, defender Javen Romero, midfielder Jon Bakero and forward Souaibou Marou, Forward Madison FC goalkeeper JT Harms and Athletic Club Boise Head Coach Nate Miller set to compete for a spot in the League One Final. 
 No. 3 seed Athletic Club Boise hosts No. 7 seed Chattanooga Red Wolves SC on Saturday night at 9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) at Athletic Club Boise Soccer Stadium, while on Sunday at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) at American Legion Memorial Stadium, the No. 1-seed Charlotte Independence take on No. 4 seed Forward Madison FC in the Semifinals of the 2026 USL League One Playoffs 
 The 2026 USL League One Awards were voted on by team management following the conclusion of the 2026 League One regular season. 
 2026 USL League One Awards 
 2026 USL League One Goalkeeper of the Year – Winner Announced Monday, Nov. 9 
 JT Harms, Forward Madison FC – A 24-year-old Wisconsin native, Harms started 31 of Madison’s 32 regular-season matches in 2026, where Madison was the only League One club to hold its opponents to fewer than one goal per game. Harms had 10 clean sheets, which tied him for the most in League One, and posted a -2.03 Goals Prevented mark while making 74 saves on a 71.3% save percentage. 
 Cole Jensen, Union Omaha – The USL League One Golden Glove award winner posted a 78.3% save percentage to lead all qualified goalkeepers. The 6-foot-5 keeper only conceded 15 goals in 17 matches started, logging a –7.16 Goals Prevented mark, where he posted five clean sheets to help Union Omaha ultimately finish second in League One in 2026. 
 Matt Levy, Charlotte Independence – The Jacks set a new League One record with 20 regular season victories en route to winning the 2026 Players’ Shield; Levy got the start in 19 of them, as the keeper’s steady play helped guide Charlotte to a first-place finish. Levy’s 102 saves and 72.5% save percentage ranked second among qualified League One keepers, and Charlotte’s keeper led the league with four penalty kicks saved and finished the regular season with a –3.68 Goals Prevented mark while averaging 1.3 goals conceded per game. 
 2026 USL League One Defender of the Year – Winner Announced Tuesday, Nov. 10 
 Samuel Owusu, Union Omaha – In his second season in Omaha, Owusu earned an All-League First Team selection as the Owls' only member of the First Team. The Ghanaian defender did so by winning 136 duels at a 64.8% success rate while also recording 118 clearances, 118 recoveries and 18 blocked shots. He had two goals scored as well, but Owusu’s defensive prowess made the 25-year-old stand out, as he logged the most minutes on Omaha (2,893) to help the side concede the second-fewest goals in all of League One. 
 Javen Romero, Charlotte Independence – Only 20 years old, Romero was a key cog in the Charlotte Independence machine in 2026. Romero had four goal contributions as the club set a new League One record with 74 goals but made his biggest contributions elsewhere; Romero led the Independence with 86 aerial duels won and 123 clearances and had the club's second-most tackles won (37) and third-highest number of interceptions (26). 
 Anderson Rosa, Sarasota Paradise – While Rosa netted the most goals of a defender in all of League One (eight), the Brazilian also added nine assists to lead the expansion club with 17 goal contributions. As one of League One’s most dangerous defenders on the attack, he was also strong across the entire field. Rosa led Sarasota with 47 tackles won, 141 duels won and 34 interceptions, showcasing himself as one of the league’s most complete players. 
 2026 USL League One Coach of the Year – Winner Announced Wednesday, Nov. 11 
 Vincenzo Candela, Union Omaha – In Candela’s first full season as the head coach of the Owls, Omaha’s 19 regular season wins were tied for the second most for a single League One season. Los Búhos finished in second place with a +20-goal differential and were one of the league’s top home clubs. Omaha only lost one home game in the 2026 season, and in the process set a League One record with a 26-match home unbeaten streak, dating back to 2025. 
 Mike Jeffries, Charlotte Independence – While the Jacks had the most wins (20), points (66) and goals scored (74) in a single League One season in 2026, Jeffries quietly made history for himself. Charlotte’s head coach became the first USL coach to surpass 150 coaching wins with a single club (USL Championship and League One), and also set a new League One record with his 65th coaching win (regular season and playoffs). 
 Nate Miller, Athletic Club Boise – In Boise’s inaugural season, Miller effectively built the club from the ground up into a contender for silverware. AC Boise finished the regular season in third place and became just the second expansion side to host a home playoff match – on Saturday night, it will become the first to host two. The first-year side posted an impressive 17-8-7 record to earn 58 points while establishing a devoted fanbase. Thanks to its success on and off the field, the club will play the 2027 season in the USL Championship. 
 2026 USL League One Young Player of the Year – Winner Announced Thursday, Nov. 12 
 Denis Krioutchenkov, One Knoxville SC – Krioutchenkov wrapped up his college career at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte, then joined League One’s defending champions and Players’ Shield winners and made an immediate impact. In his first professional match, he scored two goals in a win over Westchester SC, then went on to lead Knoxville with 11 goals and five assists, becoming the first Young Player of the Year-eligible player to log at least 10 goals and five assists in a season in League One history. The 22-year-old finished second in League One with 4.6 shots per 90 and total shots on target (43) in his first professional campaign. 
 Javen Romero, Charlotte Independence – Also a finalist for the USL League One Defender of the Year, Romero’s age-20 season saw him play well beyond his years. 2026 was far from Romero’s first bout with professional soccer, as he made his pro debut in 2021 at 15 years old with Las Vegas Lights FC in the USL Championship, then spent a few seasons with Los Angeles FC’s MLS NEXT Pro squad. In his second season with Charlotte, Romero led the Independence with 86 aerial duels won and 123 clearances. 
 Kyle Evans, Westchester SC – Evans departed from Marist University ahead of his senior season to join Westchester SC, where the 21-year-old helped Westchester SC score 55 goals, tied for the third most in League One with Union Omaha – only Forward Madison FC and Charlotte Independence, who face off in this weekend's USL League One Semifinals, scored more. Evans netted two goals and led the Golden Apples with eight assists on the season. 
 2026 USL League One Player of the Year – Winner Announced Friday, Nov. 13 
 Teddy Baker, One Knoxville SC – In his first year in Knoxville, Baker was the catalyst for the defending champions’ offense throughout the 2026 regular season. A midfielder from England, Baker’s 88 chances created were the most in all of League One, and he led his club with seven assists on the season. Additionally, Baker found the back of the net on his own with five goals this season, and distributed the ball well, completing 709 successful passes in the opponent's half. 
 Jon Bakero, Charlotte Independence – The Spaniard’s 2026 campaign will be remembered for years to come, as Bakero masterfully put together a historic year for the Jacks. Bakero’s 18 assists set a new League One record for assists in a single season, and with his eight goals, he also equaled Trevor Amann's single-season record with 26 goal contributions. Of Charlotte’s record-setting 74-goal season, Bakero had a goal contribution on more than a third of them, as he won the Golden Playmaker award. 
 Souaibou Marou, Charlotte Independence – Marou earned the USL League One Golden Boot award in 2026 thanks to a whopping 18 goals from the Cameroonian national teamer, as he doubled his nine goals scored mark in 2025. He led all of League One with 44 shots on target to lead Charlotte in its season-long goal barrage, where he picked up two braces and added a late season hat trick to pull away in the Golden Boot race.
